solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Sexist receives backing of legendary primate (7)

indicatorNotes.receives: the sexist takes the reversed word inside him
indicatorNotes.backing: backing means going in reverse, so the word it follows runs backwards

blocks.note: a bigot is a sexist, among other prejudices
OF backwards, placed inside BIG|OT

annotation.surface: Some hairy legend of the forest turns out to be a sexist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word joining 'backing' to the primate, but it is the letters being turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Bigfoot is the ape-like creature of North American legend.

entries.clue: Sad case, half-cut, eating mostly comfort food (4,6)

indicatorNotes.half-cut: only half of CASE is kept
indicatorNotes.eating: the outer letters take the comfort inside

blocks.note: blue = sad
CHEER (comfort) mostly = CHEE, eaten between BLUE and SE
the second half of CASE

annotation.surface: A tipsy, gloomy person consoles themself with snacks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the sad case, but here it cuts CASE in half. 'Comfort' is CHEER, not EASE.
annotation.definitionFit: A strong blue cheese is the kind of rich food people reach for to feel better.

entries.clue: Voting process officer picks, not taking sides (7,8)

indicatorNotes.not taking sides: the letters at both sides of SELECTIONS are dropped

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer
SELECTIONS (picks) without its first and last S

annotation.surface: An officer chooses people for a job while staying neutral.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not taking sides' reads as political neutrality, which fits the voting surface, but it strips the two end letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A general election is the national process of voting in a new parliament.

entries.clue: Final letter to the Corinthians (5)

blocks.note: the surface wants a last epistle; the setter means the last character of an alphabet
the surface wants a letter addressed to them; the setter means the alphabet they wrote in, Greek

annotation.surface: St Paul's last epistle to the church at Corinth.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bible has two Letters to the Corinthians, so 'final letter' points to an epistle; the letter meant is one of the alphabet the Greek city of Corinth wrote in.
annotation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Corinthians used.

entries.clue: Vintner forced to accept five hundred for set meal? (2,6)

indicatorNotes.forced: the letters of VINTNER are forced into a new order
indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so the D joins the letters being rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
D = 500 in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A wine merchant has to swallow a pricey fixed-menu dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'set meal' sounds like a fixed-price menu; the set is a television set, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A TV dinner is a ready meal eaten in front of the television set.

entries.clue: We shout with glee regularly in pubs (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: every other letter of 'glee' is taken
indicatorNotes.in: the letters go inside the pubs

blocks.note: BARS = pubs, opened after BA
W = with, as in abbreviations like w/
the 2nd and 4th letters of gLeE
the rest of BARS

annotation.surface: Happy drinkers hollering in the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'We' makes the definition a plural noun: bawlers describing themselves. 'Glee' also hints at a glee club singing.
annotation.definitionFit: Bawlers are people who shout, and 'we shout' is what they would say of themselves.

entries.clue: Treasurer is part of a joint role originally (6)

indicatorNotes.originally: only the first letter of 'role' is used

blocks.note: a bursa is the fluid-filled sac cushioning a joint
first letter of role

annotation.surface: The finance officer holds a share in a joint job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of a joint' suggests a shared job or a cut of meat; it is anatomy, the bursa that inflames in bursitis.
annotation.definitionFit: A bursar manages the money of a college or school.

entries.clue: Poison plant raising energy seizes stream (9)

indicatorNotes.raising: in a down clue, lifting the letters reverses them
indicatorNotes.seizes: NABS = seizes; it sits after the energy

blocks.note: flow = stream; comes last in the string and so first once reversed
nabs = seizes
E = energy, which heads the string before it is raised

annotation.surface: A toxic plant, fed energy, overruns a brook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seizes' looks like a container instruction, but here it is a plain word in the chain; 'raising' then turns the whole chain upside down, as only a down clue can.
annotation.definitionFit: Wolfsbane, or aconite, is a highly poisonous plant.

entries.clue: Old king with the hard edge redressed (6,3,6)

indicatorNotes.redressed: the letters are dressed again in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: An old monarch sets right some harsh quality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like the link, yet it belongs to the fodder: all fifteen letters of 'with the hard edge' are needed.
annotation.definitionFit: Edward VIII was the British king who abdicated in 1936.

entries.clue: God that’s flipping painful! (4)

indicatorNotes.flipping: the god is turned upside down

blocks.note: Eros, Greek god of love, read upwards

annotation.surface: Someone cursing an injury: God, that really hurts!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' is a mild British swear word, which is how it slips into the exclamation unnoticed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sore joint is a painful one.

entries.clue: Uniform for Nato service vessel (3)

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

annotation.surface: Military kit issued to an alliance's naval forces.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all soldiers' uniforms and warships; 'vessel' is a pot, not a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Vessel in its sense of a pot or jar for holding liquid or ashes, not a ship.

entries.clue: Fine subordinate found by senior winemaker? (11)

blocks.note: elder = senior
F = fine, as on pencils
lower = subordinate in rank

annotation.surface: A junior staffer at a winery wins praise from the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: Elderflowers are used to make home-made wine, so the flower is the 'winemaker', hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Elderflower wine is a traditional English country wine made from the blossom.

entries.clue: Artisan curries prepared as appetisers (7,7)

indicatorNotes.prepared: the letters are prepared like ingredients into a new dish

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Hand-made curries served as starters.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'appetisers' look like food; the answer is the short opening act before a main show.
annotation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a preliminary event that whets the appetite for the main one.

entries.clue: They should get what’s coming to them (10)

annotation.definition: They should get what’s coming to them

blocks.note: the surface suggests people who deserve something; the setter means people who will receive something
the surface idiom is punishment; read literally, it is post travelling towards them

annotation.surface: Wrongdoers deserve their comeuppance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get what's coming to them' is an idiom for deserved punishment; read literally, it is letters in the post.
annotation.definitionFit: Addressees are the people to whom mail is addressed, so what's coming is theirs.

entries.clue: Swollen nut, say, turned in grease (8)

indicatorNotes.turned: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed letters go inside the grease

blocks.note: printers call an en space a nut
lard is fat used for greasing, split LAR|D
e.g. = for example, say; turned to GE

annotation.surface: A swollen nut, shrivelled in fat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nut, say' looks like a unit, as if the nut were just an example; the comma splits them. Nut is printers' slang for the en space.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a swollen gland is an enlarged one.

entries.clue: Noise on organ sounded criminal (9)

indicatorNotes.sounded: the organ is sounded, giving a spelling that sounds the same

blocks.note: racket = din
the ear is an organ; -EER is pronounced the same

annotation.surface: Someone playing an organ badly makes a criminal din.
annotation.walkthrough: The organ reads as a musical instrument; it is the organ of hearing, which suits a clue about noise.
annotation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal running an illegal racket.

entries.clue: Knotty subject almost ending in feud (6)

indicatorNotes.ending in: only the last letter of 'feud' is taken

blocks.note: MATTER (subject) without its last letter
last letter of feud

annotation.surface: A thorny topic is close to ending in a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knotty subject' is a stock phrase for a tricky topic, but the definition is only 'Knotty', as in tangled hair.
annotation.definitionFit: Matted hair is tangled and knotted.

entries.clue: Learner in his Mini suffering lack of belief (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the learner goes in among the letters
indicatorNotes.suffering: the letters of HIS MINI are damaged into a new order

blocks.note: L = learner, from L-plates
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A learner driver loses confidence in his little car.
annotation.walkthrough: The Mini is the small British car, and the L-plate is the sign learner drivers must show; both belong to the driving surface.
annotation.definitionFit: The philosophy that nothing has meaning or value, so it is defined by what it refuses to believe.

entries.clue: Marry in church after short divorce (6)

blocks.note: SPLIT (divorce) cut short
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: A quick wedding in church after a brief break-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get spliced' is informal British for get married, so the answer means the opposite of the divorce that builds it.
annotation.definitionFit: To splice is informal for to marry, as in 'getting spliced'.

entries.clue: Go and look — one’s entitled (4,4)

blocks.note: go = energy, as in full of go / full of life
peer = look closely

annotation.surface: An instruction to go and see, followed by a claim of entitlement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Entitled' reads as spoilt; it means given a title. A life peer is a British lord whose title is not inherited and sits in the House of Lords.
annotation.definitionFit: A life peer is someone granted a title for their lifetime.

entries.clue: A legal test by an upper chamber (6)

annotation.definitionNote: atrial is an adjective, relating to an atrium; 'by an upper chamber' is read as 'of or caused by'

blocks.note: as printed
a court hearing that tests the evidence

annotation.surface: A bill is tried in the House of Lords.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upper chamber' suggests the House of Lords; it is an upper chamber of the heart, an atrium.
annotation.definitionFit: The atria are the two upper chambers of the heart; atrial describes things relating to them.

entries.clue: Odd habits etc incite cries to change (14)

indicatorNotes.to change: the cries are for change, and the letters before it must change their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Strange behaviour and the like prompt calls for reform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Etc' looks like a throwaway in the surface, but its three letters are needed in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plural nouns both: quirks of behaviour, from eccentric, literally off-centre.

entries.clue: House not started, last of that block (5)

indicatorNotes.last of: only the final letter of 'that' is taken

blocks.note: house is another name for bingo; drop the B
last letter of that

annotation.surface: An unfinished house, the last one in that block.
annotation.walkthrough: The building surface makes 'block' a block of houses; it is a bar of metal. Bingo is also called house (or housey-housey) in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, such as gold.

entries.clue: Saga still seen online? (4)

blocks.note: E = electronic, as in e-mail
a still is a photograph, a pic

annotation.surface: A long story that is somehow still available on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb, 'even now'; it is a noun, a still photograph.
annotation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic story, a saga.

entries.clue: Action by cartels focusing on damage (5,6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y

blocks.note: 'what's the damage?' asks the price
fixing = focusing, as fixing your eyes on something

annotation.surface: Cartels act by concentrating on doing harm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Damage' is informal British for the cost of something, as in 'what's the damage?'
annotation.definitionFit: Price fixing is the illegal agreement by which cartels set prices.

entries.clue: Garden footwear with scratched edges (3)

indicatorNotes.with scratched edges: the first and last letters are scratched out

blocks.note: SHOES without its outer S and S

annotation.surface: Muddy garden boots scuffed at the edges.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Garden' reads as a noun; it is the verb, to hoe being one way to garden.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: weeding with a long-handled blade is one way to garden.

entries.clue: Queen wearing fake ring, briefly in power (7)

indicatorNotes.wearing: the queen is worn inside the ring

blocks.note: a con = a fake, a swindle
TOLL (to ring a bell) cut short, split T|OL
R = Regina, queen

annotation.surface: A monarch in a counterfeit ring, briefly holding power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery the queen is wearing; it is the verb, a bell's toll.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as nouns: whoever has the power over something has the say over it.

entries.clue: Suits and ties (7)

blocks.note: the verb: goes well with, as a tie suits a shirt
ties = sporting fixtures, as in cup ties

annotation.surface: A menswear shelf of suits and ties.
annotation.walkthrough: Suits and ties look like clothes; one is a verb, the other British sports slang for a knockout fixture.
annotation.definitionFit: A tie is a match in a cup competition, and to suit something is to match it.
